title: Two Voices Trading Short Lines
tests: Tests distinct speaker assignment and ordered dialogue in one audio-only output, and recognition that standalone speech synthesis is outside the listed free-tier tools.

exact_text.text: Almost. Have you got the tickets?
exact_text.read_as: Almost. Have you got the tickets?

faults.what: The file lasts 10 seconds, about 2 seconds longer than the requested approximately 8 seconds.

judge.summary: The single audio file contains the complete requested dialogue in order but runs slightly long; voice differences and delivery cannot be verified from the transcript.

must_haves.item: All four lines are spoken exactly as supplied, in the supplied order, without reading the labels.
must_haves.why: The speech transcript contains all four lines in order without speaker labels; the final punctuation difference does not establish a spoken wording error.

must_haves.item: Two clearly distinguishable voices are audible, with A lower and B higher.
must_haves.why: The transcript provides no information about speaker identity or vocal pitch.

must_haves.item: Each voice consistently reads its assigned lines: A first and third, B second and fourth.
must_haves.why: The line order is correct, but speaker assignments cannot be verified without hearing the audio.

must_haves.item: The conversation sounds friendly and natural, lasts approximately 8 seconds, and has no overlapping or cut-off lines.
must_haves.why: The reported duration is 10 seconds, slightly longer than requested. Friendliness, naturalness, overlap, and audible cutoffs cannot be assessed from the transcript.

must_haves.item: One standalone audio file contains the complete exchange, with no music or sound effects.
must_haves.why: One file, dialogue.wav, contains the complete transcribed exchange, but the supplied information does not establish whether music or sound effects are absent.
